Hills, T.P., Sceats, M., Rennie, D. and Fennell, P. (2017). LEILAC: Low cost CO2 capture for the cement and lime industries. Energy Procedia, 114, 6166-6170 (13th International Conference on Greenhouse Gas Control Technologies, GHGT-13, Lausanne, 14-18 November 2016). doi:10.1016/j.egypro.2017.03.1753

Locators are printed page numbers (6166-6170). A 5-page conference paper written before the pilot ran: it holds design claims, not measured data. The capital cost is stated only qualitatively ('no extra capital cost apart from compression'; no number), and energy use only as 'not expected to change much', so no capex or SEC rows exist. Loaded: calcination temperature, pilot size, capture and reduction shares, and the amine cost range (itself reprinted from Hills et al. 2016, ES&T). Not loaded: project timeline, consortium. The paper's 'around 60% of total direct CO2' is 95% of process CO2 (about two thirds of cement kiln CO2).
